title: Avalanche Industries - security scope & deployment options
next_steps: Jordan to share SOC2 and ISO artifacts link by 2026-11-18
Priya to run a short dedicated latency benchmark with AVAX sample prompts (2-3 days)
Customer to confirm data residency requirement and list of PII types by 2026-11-19
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (CTO - Avalanche), Lisa Ortega (Head of Security - Avalanche), Samir Patel (Cloud Architect - Avalanche)

Summary:
Quick intake to understand Avalanche's security requirements and whether Redwood Hosted, Dedicated or Private makes sense for their regulated manufacturing telemetry use case. Primary concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC for internal teams, audit log retention and encryption/KMS (HSM for key wraps). They also want EU data residency and long retention windows for logs.

Topics:
- Compliance artifacts (SOC2 Type II, ISO27001)
- Authentication (SSO/SAML, SCIM provisioning)
- Authorization (RBAC, role separation)
- Audit logs & retention (7+ years, tamper-evident)
- Encryption & KMS (customer-managed keys, HSM)
- Deployment options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC / on-prem)
- Latency/cost tradeoffs and fallback policies

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we've got about 45 minutes, so we'll run through high level security intake and then Priya will jump into some deployment detail and latency/cost tradeoffs. Mark, do you want to kick off with a very quick intro to the data flows you care about?
[00:18] Mark: Sure, yeah. So Avalanche is ingesting device telemetry and then we run models for predictive maintenance. The outputs sometimes include machine IDs and occasionally owner contact info, so it's PII-ish, right. Our big ask is we need auditability and strict data residency — EU only for this set. Also our legal team is going to want to see SOC2 Type II and any ISO certificates you have.
[00:36] Lisa: Sorry to interrupt, and just to add: we need logs retained for compliance for up to seven years. Also we want tamper evidence and chain of custody for audit trails.
[00:49] Jordan: Yep understood. Priya, do you want to speak to how Redwood surfaces audit logs and retention in the Hosted and Dedicated products?
[00:57] Priya: Sure. So for Hosted we provide tenant-level audit logs accessible via the Console and via an API. Logs include request metadata, model variant, tokens consumed, and user identity markers. Retention defaults are 90 days for hosted, but we have extended retention add-ons and enterprise plans where we can push to customer-managed S3 or to a secure archive for longer retention. For Dedicated you can configure local log collectors, and for Private deployments logs remain inside the VPC and can be forwarded to the customer's SIEM.
[01:28] Samir: When you say customer-managed S3 for long retention, is that encrypted server-side? Who holds the keys? We have to use our HSM-backed KMS for anything over 1 year per policy.
[01:39] Priya: Good question. We support customer-managed keys via KMS. For Hosted we integrate with AWS KMS or GCP KMS using a customer key alias; we can also integrate with HSM-backed key stores in enterprise setups. For Dedicated we can offer a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flow where keys never leave your control. For Private/on-prem we can configure local HSMs; that's the most isolated option. Full key-rotation and access logs are available.
[02:06] Lisa: Is the KMS integration full crypto-in-transit and at-rest, and is the envelope key in HSM?
[02:12] Priya: Yes, TLS in transit. At rest we use envelope encryption; the data encryption keys are wrapped by your KMS key which can be an HSM-protected key. In Hosted there's an extra layer where Redwood's storage is encrypted and the DEKs can be wrapped by your KMS. I will clarify the exact HSM attestation we support and drop the SOC2 artifact.
[02:33] Jordan: Lisa, you mentioned tamper evidence — do you need write-once retention or just cryptographic integrity proofs?
[02:39] Lisa: Prefer cryptographic integrity proofs plus append-only logs. If the system can show immutability for audit events that's good.
[02:47] Priya: We can stream to an append-only store and produce signed checksums for audit snapshots. For Dedicated and Private deployments customers often forward logs to their own write-once S3 buckets with object lock for legal hold.
[03:01] Mark: OK. On SSO, we use Azure AD and expect SAML-based SSO plus SCIM for provisioning roles. How granular is your RBAC? We want separation between ops, analytics, and product.
[03:12] Jordan: Priya, maybe you can walk RBAC and SAML.
[03:16] Priya: Sure. We support SAML 2.0 SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and we expose role templates. You can map AD groups to Redwood roles and we support a least-privilege model — separate roles for admin, deploy, read-only analytics, and developer. For Dedicated you can also bring custom roles and integrate with an external IAM. One caveat: Hosted supports SCIM provisioning in enterprise plans; smaller hosted tenants might require manual assignment.
[03:43] Samir: If we go Dedicated but hosted in your cloud, will we still get SSO and our SCIM connector? Any latency to the SCIM calls?
[03:51] Priya: SCIM is standard REST calls; latency is negligible. For Dedicated in a customer VPC or our dedicated fleet you can choose to have the SCIM connector inside your network to minimize roundtrip.
[04:03] Lisa: Are there certifications or SOC2 reports we can review? We have to sign an NDA typically but we'd like to see Type II and the period.
[04:12] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll share the SOC2 Type II report and ISO27001 cert — I'll get those links into the deck and send them to Mark and Lisa after the call.
[04:20] Mark: Great. Also curious about data residency: if we use Hosted, can you guarantee EU-only processing and storage? We run in multiple regions but this data set must remain in EU.
[04:31] Priya: For Hosted we have regional tenancy. We can pin models to EU regions and ensure storage and compute are in EU zones. For Dedicated we can place the pool in EU-only hardware; Private of course gives full control. There are sometimes peripheral services (like metrics ingestion) that may be in control plane regions; we can arrange for a private control plane for enterprise customers. We'll call that out in the security docs.
[04:57] Samir: One of our concerns is model fallbacks. If your primary EU capacity is saturated and requests are routed to a cheaper global capacity, how do we prevent data from leaving EU?
[05:07] Priya: We can set routing policies to never route out of EU for that tenant. By default we do soft fallbacks for availability. For strict data residency you can pin strict routing policy and Redwood will fail requests rather than fallback out of region.
[05:20] Mark: OK that helps. On retention, 7 years is long. Any issues with egress charges if we archive logs to our S3?
[05:29] Jordan: That's usually customer-managed costs. If Redwood is piping logs to your S3, those egress costs depend on whether data moves across cloud providers. We'll document expected flows.
[05:39] Lisa: Audit trail visibility — do you provide immutable snapshots we can hand to auditors, or do auditors need Redwood access?
[05:46] Priya: We can provide export bundles (signed) and auditor access via time-limited roles. For enterprise accounts we can also create read-only audit dumps pushed to customer S3 with a signed manifest. That tends to satisfy auditors.
[06:01] Samir: About encryption key rotation — if we rotate keys, do you rewrap all DEKs automatically? What's the window?
[06:08] Priya: We support key rotation flows where DEKs get rewrapped; the process is background and depends on dataset size — usually minutes to a few hours for active keys. For very large archives we recommend a migration window.
[06:20] Mark: Let's talk threat model: do you support customer-managed HSMs (nshield or YubiHSM) or just cloud KMS? We need FIPS and PKCS#11 compatibility.
[06:31] Priya: For Hosted we support AWS CloudHSM via KMS integration and external HSMs via partner connectors. For Dedicated we can integrate with on-prem HSMs over secure tunnels and support PKCS#11. We'll surface the compatibility matrix in the follow-up.
[06:48] Jordan: Any other compliance checks — ISO 27001, GDPR DSR handling?
[06:53] Lisa: Yes, GDPR DSRs — we need a documented process for data deletion and proof of deletion.
[06:59] Priya: We have DSR processes for Hosted and Dedicated; for Private deployments deletion is managed by the customer. For Hosted we can return deletion receipts and show logs demonstrating deletion. We'll include sample policies.
[07:14] Mark: On the security assessment side — do you provide penetration test results or a summary?
[07:20] Jordan: We can share redacted pentest summaries; for full pentest reports we usually require an NDA and sometimes a security questionnaire process.
[07:30] Samir: Speaking of questionnaires — we use a 300+ control security questionnaire. How do you prefer to handle that? Do you have a collated answers doc?
[07:38] Priya: We maintain an information security pack and a prefilled questionnaire for common frameworks. For anything custom we can work through the security engineering team. We can also run a live Q&A with our security lead if you want to go deeper.
[07:52] Lisa: That would be useful — maybe a follow-up technical deep dive with your security lead and our compliance officer.
[07:59] Jordan: Absolutely. We'll schedule that.
[08:03] Mark: One more thing — incident response. If there's a suspected data leakage we need notification SLA and a post-incident report. What's Redwood's timeline?
[08:12] Priya: We have an incident response playbook. Notification windows depend on severity; for P1 leaks we notify within one hour and provide a detailed root cause within 72 hours. We also offer live war-room support on enterprise plans.
[08:26] Lisa: Are those SLAs contractual?
[08:29] Jordan: For Dedicated and Private customers with enterprise contracts we have contractual SLAs. Hosted standard tier has best-effort, enterprise hosted tiers include defined SLAs.
[08:39] Samir: Network isolation: for Dedicated can we restrict egress to a defined set of IPs and have private peering?
[08:46] Priya: Yes — we support VPC peering, private endpoints, and allowlist egress rules for Dedicated. Private deployment is fully under your network controls.
[08:56] Mark: About model artifacts — do you store model weights or are those ephemeral? For IP reasons we need to ensure models we use for inference are not mixed with other tenants.
[09:05] Priya: Model binaries in Hosted are tenant-scoped where possible, but some shared layers may be cached for efficiency. For Dedicated we can pin specific model versions to your pool and ensure isolation. Private is fully separated. We'll note the isolation levels in the documentation.
[09:20] Jordan: Quick question from me: you mentioned manufacturing telemetry; what's the acceptable latency SLO for inference?
[09:25] Mark: Sub-200ms p99 for short prompts is ideal. For batch offline jobs longer windows are fine. But any bursty high-throughput use needs to be cost predictable.
[09:35] Priya: Sub-200ms p99 is doable on optimized Dedicated pools depending on model size and quantization. Hosted latency varies by model and region; part of Redwood Optimize is runtime recommendations like quantized variants or batching policies to meet your p99 while keeping cost down.
[09:52] Samir: Could you do a quick sketch of cost delta between Hosted and Dedicated for our expected profile? We can share sample traffic but rough ballpark would help.
[10:01] Jordan: We'll follow up with a cost worksheet after we get sample prompts and QPS. Priya will run a benchmark so we'll have real numbers.
[10:10] Lisa: On the legal side, any support for data processing agreements and standard DPAs? We need to review those too.
[10:16] Jordan: Yes we have standard DPA templates; AE will share them.
[10:20] Mark: I also want to understand retention and deletion of KV cache — our prompts include previous history and we need selective retention and TTLs.
[10:28] Priya: We can configure KV cache TTLs and prefix caching behavior. For PII you can opt out of caching or use differential TTLs. We also support prompt filtering to redact before storage in some deployments.
[10:41] Samir: A little nit: earlier you said default hosted log retention is 90 days, but can you produce a signed archive of the audit log monthly to our S3? That'd satisfy our auditors.
[10:50] Priya: Yes, we can push monthly signed archives to your S3 or to a third-party archive with object lock for the 7-year window. There's usually a storage+ingest fee.
[10:59] Lisa: For access controls, do you support MFA enforced for all admin roles?
[11:04] Priya: Yes we enforce MFA and can require hardware keys for admins.
[11:09] Mark: On the topic of data deletion proofs — you mentioned deletion receipts. Can you show an example?
[11:15] Priya: We'll include a sample deletion receipt in the follow-up package — it's basically a signed manifest with a checksum and a log of delete operations.
[11:23] Jordan: Great. Any other open concerns?
[11:26] Lisa: One question: are you SOC2 controls mapped to ISO clauses and to specific encryptions and processes? Our audit team likes to see a mapping matrix.
[11:35] Priya: We have a controls mapping matrix that maps SOC2 controls to ISO and to our technical controls. We'll include that.
[11:42] Samir: We also want a list of third-party subprocessors and their roles — for instance which cloud providers host which components.
[11:49] Jordan: We'll include a subprocessor list and region mapping.
[11:55] Mark: Finally, for a pilot we'd like a short Dedicated trial in EU region with BYOK and 2-week benchmarking. Can Redwood provision that?
[12:03] Priya: Yes, we can provision a short-duration Dedicated pool for evaluation. We'll need a sample dataset and a scoped QPS estimate. We'll limit model sizes and provide a benchmark report.
[12:15] Jordan: OK perfect. Let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[12:19] Jordan: Action items recap — Jordan to send SOC2/ISO artifacts and DPA, Priya to run dedicated latency benchmark and provide compatibility matrix for HSMs, customer to confirm data residency binding and sample prompts. Schedule a security deep dive next week with our security lead. Anything to add?
[12:38] Mark: That's it from us. Thanks.
[12:41] Lisa: Thanks all.
[12:43] Jordan: Thanks team, we'll follow up with the package by Wednesday.

Notes on transcription errors: occasionally SAML read as 'Samual', KV cache sometimes transcribed 'K V cache', and some product names truncated. There was minor crosstalk at ~00:49 when Lisa interjected.
